  • Experience with Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) interconnects, including fluid quick-connect couplings, electrical busway tie-ins, and high-density fiber topologies.
  • Experience architecting formal closed-loop corrective action processes (e.g., FRACAS, 8D) that convert jobsite assembly challenges into upstream factory design modifications.

title: Filestore Tech Leader
descriptionHtml:

Google Cloud's Filestore is the foundational, high-performance managed file storage service powering enterprise applications and the next wave of AI/ML and Agentic workloads. Serving thousands of customers with strict durability and ultra-low latency guarantees, Filestore is undergoing a major technical evolution—building next-generation multi-tenant distributed storage engines and deep integrations with Kubernetes and AI orchestration platforms.

As a Senior Staff Software Engineer and Technical Lead, you will serve as a primary architectural lead for critical segments of the Filestore distributed storage stack. You will address distributed systems challenges from first principles: designing lock-free high-throughput data paths, high-density architectures (supporting tens of thousands of shares per instance), dynamic resource management, and sub-millisecond I/O paths. You will partner closely with engineering managers, product leaders, and sister teams across Compute, Networking, and GKE to shape a multi-year technical roadmap, elevate engineering excellence across the site, and mentor executive technical leaders.

Google Cloud accelerates every organization’s ability to digitally transform its business and industry. We deliver enterprise-grade solutions that leverage Google’s cutting-edge technology, and tools that help developers build more sustainably. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted partner to enable growth and solve their most critical business problems.

Responsibilities

  • Define the multi-year technical goal and architectural roadmap for Filestore's core distributed storage engine, balancing rapid innovation with durability, availability, and multi-tenant isolation.
  • Architect and implement high-performance, distributed filesystem backends optimized for emerging AI/ML training, inference, and Agentic workloads requiring massive concurrency, extreme density, and low-latency data access.
  • Partner with Product Management, SRE, and adjacent Google Cloud teams (Compute Engine, Kubernetes/GKE, Andromeda Networking, Hardware/TI) to drive technical consensus and solve complex cross-stack integration issues.
  • Advocate first-party service reliability by establishing rigorous SLAs/SLIs, system modeling, performance benchmarking, fault injection, and zero-downtime rolling upgrades across global fleets.
  • Act as a multiplier by coaching and developing other Tech Leads, fostering a culture of engineering, deep code reviews, and proactive technical debt management.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 8 years of experience in the IT Industry with building and developing large-scale infrastructure or distributed systems.
  • Experience with software development in one or more programming languages (e.g., Python, C, C++, Java, Javascript).
  • Experience with Storage storage, databases, file systems, virtualization, or networking.
  • Experience in a technical leadership role.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience in building relevant benchmarks, performance optimization, tuning, and profiling large-scale distributed infrastructure for low latency and high throughput.
  • Experience leading large, cross-geography engineering teams, mentoring senior technical talent, and successfully engaging with large-scale enterprise customers. Presenting and driving decision and consensus with senior technical and business leadership.
  • Understanding of evolving AI/ML workloads (training, inference, agentic) combined with a proven track record of building highly durable, massive-scale distributed storage systems.
  • Strong background in building complex, multi-tenant distributed systems from scratch, with the ability to model and optimize system behavior from first principles.

  • 2 years of software development or ML research experience, or education equivalent credit (e.g., internships, student research, pre-graduate working experience).
  • Experience conducting research to solve problems in AI or ML.
  • Experience in implementing machine learning algorithms or techniques (e.g., basicautomatic differentiation) and in using machine learning frameworks (e.g., Jax, PyTorch, Triton).
  • Experience designing and operating distributed computing systems for large-scale AI/ML workloads.
  • One or more scientific publication submission(s) for conferences, journals, or public repositories, including publications on machine learning or computational neuroscience.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience with distributed storage systems, relational databases, and schema or query design (e.g., PostgreSQL, Cloud Spanner, Bigtable, Cassandra, or DynamoDB).
  • Experience with large-scale data pipelines and distributed batch or streaming frameworks (e.g., Apache Beam, Spark, Dataflow, Ray, or Flink).
  • Prior experience building data infrastructure, pipelines, or tooling within an ML research environment.
  • Familiarity with a compiled systems/backend language (such as C++, Rust, Go, or Java) or media codecs (video, audio, image).

title: Technical Program Manager, AI for Science
descriptionHtml:
Artificial intelligence will be one of humanity’s most transformative inventions. At DeepMind, we are a pioneering AI lab with exceptional interdisciplinary teams focused on advancing AI development to solve complex global challenges and accelerate high-quality product innovation for billions of users. We use our technologies for widespread public benefit and scientific discovery, ensuring safety and ethics are always our highest priority.

We are pushing the boundaries across multiple domains. Our global teams offer diverse learning opportunities and varied career pathways for those driven to achieve exceptional results through collective effort.

Responsibilities

  • Lead and shape complex programs at the intersection of foundational models, AI agents, and scientific research within DeepMind’s SSI Initiatives Unit.
  • Act as a trusted thought partner to research, engineering leads, product managers, and the wider program management team.
  • Help navigate the deep ambiguity inherent in breakthrough scientific research through strong program definition, execution, and technical delivery.
  • Drive the integration of autonomous agents, reasoning loops, and sandboxed research tooling into scientific workflows.
  • Collaborate across research pillars, from biology and quantum chemistry to automated theorem proving and compute infrastructure. Ensure scientific teams have the operational rhythm, technical alignment, and resource access needed to maximize research velocity.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Computational Biology, Physics, a related quantitative/scientific discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5 years of experience in technical program management, engineering program management, or technical leadership in advanced research, machine learning, or distributed systems environments.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Demonstrated experience partnering directly with research scientists or technical leads to translate exploratory, ambiguous initiatives into concrete execution roadmaps.
  • Strong conceptual grasp of modern AI/ML systems (e.g., large language models, multi-agent frameworks, or scientific computing pipelines) and the ability to evaluate technical trade-offs.
  • Exceptional technical communication and stakeholder management skills, with a track record of driving cross-functional consensus across multidisciplinary teams.
  • A deep passion for accelerating scientific discovery, clean energy, and health through artificial intelligence.

title: GSOC SSC Program Manager, EMEA
descriptionHtml:
From keeping Googlers safe and secure to managing disruptive incidents and crises, the ability to anticipate, deter, detect, and act are the pillars of Google’s Global Security and Resilience Services (GSRS) team. As a member of GSRS you will help develop a culture where safety, security and resiliency are integrated into every facet of Google, including the creative process. You will help us continually identify, evaluate and monitor enterprise risks that could affect business activities and provide business leaders the information they need to make critical decisions. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams to create innovative strategies and develop programs that drive sustainable effectiveness.

The Global Security Operations Center is GSRS’s 24/7 ecosystem for intake, triage, management and escalation of physical security incidents and threats.

As a Security Service Center (SSC) Program Manager, you will lead the development and improvement of the Security Service Center ecosystem, a globally distributed network of more than twenty hubs operated by vendor partners managing the detection, triage and response to physical security threats to Google people and assets. This role works to ensure that the program scales effectively to enable the GSOC to deliver its mission.

Responsibilities

  • Coordinate complex and highly cross-functional projects and strategic initiatives to optimize and scale our ability to detect, assess, and mitigate risk while ensuring alignment with broader security efforts.
  • Lead the GSOC Global Security Service Centre (SSC) Program.
  • Maintain the network of distributed SSC’s in support of GSRS operations.
  • Document, analyze and regularly review SSC operations to enhance the delivery of operations.
  • Collaborate with security operations teams in the strategy and design of security service centers, with daily activities delegated and managed by the local campus or cluster security manager.

Minimum qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 10 years of experience implementing security resilience programs impacting teams across multiple regions.
  • Experience with multidisciplinary program management in an organization.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience in vendor management and vendor performance management.
  • Ability to analyze business objectives and strategies by proactively identifying impactful opportunities or gaps in systems and workflows.
  • Ability to identify, build, improve, or optimize relevant business processes.
  • Ability to lead projects by navigating priorities, measurable objectives, dependencies, planning, resourcing, scheduling, budgeting, implementation and subsequent monitoring.
  • High ethical standards with demonstrated ability to handle highly confidential and sensitive information.
  • Excellent judgement, discretion and diplomacy skills.
